books.section: Topic 6.11 Reform in the Gilded Age
Industrialization, Corporate Consolidation, and the Gospel of Wealth

primary_sources: Coxey’s Army photograph, 1894; Coney Island trade card, about 1885–1896

stimulus.text: Image 1: An 1894 photograph shows a column of men marching down a dirt road toward Washington, carrying banners. One banner reads “More Money! Less Misery! Good Roads!” A placard shows a portrait with the words “Death to Interest on Bonds.” The caption reads “Coxey’s Army approaching Washington.” Image 2: A color trade card from about 1885–1896, “Scene at Coney Island,” shows boys in suits digging in the sand on a crowded beach, with a sailboat and a paddle steamer on the water and amusement buildings, a tall tower, and an elephant-shaped hotel behind them.
stimulus.source_note: Image 1: 1894 stereograph, Library of Congress (LC-DIG-stereo-1s09209), public domain; image viewed by the writer (shared pool: u6/original-u6-coxeys-army-approaching-washington.jpg). Image 2: chromolithograph trade card, Lindner, Eddy and Clauss, New York, about 1885-1896, public domain; image viewed by the writer (shared pool: u6/u6-coney-island-scene.jpg).

stem: Image 2 shows well-dressed children at play on a crowded beach. What change in American life does this image best illustrate?

options.text: The end of child labor in factories
options.misconception: The image shows children at play, but it cannot prove that child labor had ended.

options.text: The closing of the western frontier
options.misconception: A beach scene says nothing about the frontier.

options.text: Commercial leisure for the middle class

options.misconception: Coney Island is a crowded resort near New York, so it shows city life growing, not declining.

rationales.A: Children at play do not prove that child labor had ended.
rationales.B: The beach and its amusements have nothing to do with the frontier.
rationales.C: A crowded resort with amusements, hotels, and steamers is leisure sold to paying visitors.
rationales.D: A crowded resort beside a great city shows urban life growing, not declining.
rationales.general:
Ask who the beach is for.
1. The children wear good suits, and the beach is crowded with visitors.
2. Behind them stand amusement buildings, a tower, and a hotel shaped like an elephant.
3. Those are businesses selling fun, not a wild shore.
4. Background from the books: streetcars, wages, and free time built a middle-class world of resorts and amusements.
Remember: when fun has a ticket and a hotel, leisure has become a business.
